residual.wall: Material knobs are a dimmer stack (roughness, clearcoat, pearl, absorption, key) that do not speak one dialect. Dual: dimmer-stack = principled-layer-stack.

question: What is the Disney Principled BRDF/BSDF as a complete dialect, which layers are lawful on Gasper’s dielectric gel cage, and how do prior PBR / SSS / aniso packets sit inside it?
coordinateSpaces: Cage φ, view-fixed lights, intensity-only (D-0033). FACE_CANON off this organ. Parameters are unitless [0,1] except IOR. Energy: each layer’s integral is bounded; layers add, they do not multiply opacity.
physicalLaw: Principled = one artist dialect over Cook–Torrance + a designed diffuse. Not a new physics. Burley 2012 BRDF, Burley 2015 BSDF.
Disney 2012 knobs: baseColor, subsurface, metallic, specular, specularTint, roughness, anisotropic, sheen, sheenTint, clearcoat, clearcoatGloss.
Disney 2015 adds: specTrans, scatterDistance, ior, thin. Subsurface becomes a real BSSRDF slot (normalized diffusion).
Diffuse (Burley): fd = (base/π) (1+(F90−1)(1−nL)⁵)(1+(F90−1)(1−nV)⁵), F90 = 0.5 + 2 r (h·L)². Retro-reflect at grazing. Not Lambert.
Specular: GTR2 / anisotropic GGX. α = r². F0 from specular knob: F0 = 0.08·specular²  (0.5 → 0.02; Disney later ~0.04 at 0.5). Dielectric.
Metallic: lerp to a model with no diffuse and F0 = baseColor. Gasper metallic = 0 always.
Clearcoat: second GTR lobe, F0=0.04, α_coat from clearcoatGloss (1 → α≈0.1). Amount = clearcoat.
Sheen: grazing cloth term. Not energy-primary. Gel does not need it at rest.
Subsurface knob in 2012 is a *shape* mix, not transport. 2015 scatterDistance is the real ld. Our SSS Explore is the 2015 slot.
Anisotropic: aspect = √(1−0.9a), αx=r²/aspect, αy=r²·aspect. Our aniso Explore is this knob, sourced from φ stretch.
Energy: layers add. Roughness never multiplies opacity. A dimmer is not a BRDF.
artisticLaw: Dark pearl. Intensity-only. No new hue. No chrome.
specularTint and sheenTint are hue. Forbidden (D-0033).
Rest: anisotropic 0. Coat is the gel skin. Face off this organ.
Existing bindings keep their names. They must *mean* Disney, not scale opacity.
Explore does not recut the painter.

uncertainty: Whether Burley diffuse (retro) reads on a dark pearl vs Lambert*(1−F).
Whether specular (F0 scale) is worth a knob or stays 0.5 / 0.04.
Whether clearcoatGloss needs a slider or stays 0.1.
How much pearl should tint *diffuse* vs stay a volume (SSS) color.
tests: roughness 0.1 vs 0.8 changes D, not a uniform opacity multiply.
clearcoat 0 ≡ one lobe. clearcoat 1 adds a sharp second peak.
Disney diffuse optional: if on, grazing retro > Lambert; if off, Lambert*(1−F).
SSS gain 0 + aniso 0 + coat 0 → identity with current GGX path.
FACE_CANON eye span 72. No new hue in computed fills.
visualConsequences: Same Gasper, one material language. Dials do what Disney artists expect.
Roughness = highlight width. Clearcoat = gel skin. Pearl = volume, not a brighter fill.
Absorption becomes σa / scatterDistance, not a dimmer.
Stretch streaks spec (aniso packet). Thin W transmits (SSS packet).
No chrome. No cloth sheen. No painted slash.
implementation: Explore only. Do not recut the painter this receipt.
If Work: adopt Disney as the *name* of the live stack. Do not add every knob.
Lawful live set: roughness → α, clearcoat → coat amount, pearl → diffuse/volume intensity, absorption → σa when SSS lands.
Keep metallic 0, specTrans 0, no tints, no sheen, no emission.
Optional next: Burley diffuse replace Lambert*(1−F); clearcoatGloss; specular as F0 scale.
Aniso and SSS stay their packets. They plug into this dialect. They are not a second material.
Delete 1−0.18r and any opacity-as-material remaining on this path.
